A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching title and authors. All 22 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v3, including their appendices, support comparison despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 presents theoretical definitions, guarantees, proofs, and a literature review. Empirical successes discussed in Appendix A are attributed to other works; no original empirical results are reported.

after.justification: V3 remains theoretical throughout the main text and appendices. Rollout sampling is an assumed learning model, Figure 1 is illustrative, and estimating the theoretical quantities from real traces is proposed as future work.

M1.justification: The analyzed learning procedure changes substantially. V1 specifies squared-loss empirical risk minimization in Theorem 6 and a net-based Lipschitz-extension estimator in Appendix F; v3 specifies depth-wise minimax absolute-error regression on sampled query pairs, followed by greedy selection within concentration sets (Assumption 3.1). Greedy scoring already existed, but the central training objective and estimator construction change.

E1.justification: Neither version actually trains or evaluates on datasets or benchmarks. References to miniF2F, LeanDojo, and other environments describe prior work, not experimental coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against its proposed framework. Added discussions of other theorem-proving systems are related work, not baseline comparisons.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an experimental evaluation protocol. Changes to sampling distributions, symbolic label budgets, and regression assumptions concern the theoretical learning model rather than executed experiments.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, or empirical supplementary analyses. The easy/hard-instance discussions and scaling arguments are theoretical interpretations, not new tests.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Their probability bounds and independent-label assumptions are mathematical statements rather than empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Neither version contains original empirical measurements, performance rankings, or observed result entries. Revised provability bounds and statistical rates are theoretical changes assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V3 specializes the stochastic-MDP framework to deterministic verifier dynamics, adds faithful-abstraction equivalence with syntactic provability (Proposition 2.2), and proves occupancy-weighted regret and conditional-success bounds. Its regression theorem uses explicit i.i.d. coverage and minimax-estimation assumptions. V1's adaptive-deviation result and detailed certificate and measure-compactness proofs are omitted, although certificate and truncation ideas remain in v3's appendices.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion shift from broad score-guided planning, Bellman certificates, and sequential complexity to an offline-regression-plus-greedy guarantee. Faithful correspondence with syntactic provability and the learned prover's average truncated proof length become central claimed contributions.

C2.justification: V3 substantially sharpens applicability and interpretation: it distinguishes learned-policy occupancy from optimal proof length, explains candidate-retention requirements and instability when a prover leaves the covered region, and identifies oracle rollout labels and exact regression as idealizations. Its limitations explicitly separate the analyzed greedy pipeline from practical beam search, backtracking, repair, and multi-agent systems.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies an implementation, concrete hyperparameter configuration, hardware/runtime measurements, or code/data access information. The revised symbolic sampling and estimator specifications are methodological and theoretical changes.

R1.justification: Most theorem-proving and test-time-scaling literature coverage is retained. V3 adds targeted positioning against Bourbaki, Amit et al.'s verifiability theory, and Sonoda et al.'s hierarchical-prover analysis, plus Lean 4 and cut-complexity references. Several anecdotal and sequential-complexity references from v1 are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, theoretical narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around one principal learning guarantee. Eleven main sections become seven; related work enters the main text, proofs are consolidated in Appendix A, and truncation and representation-learning material move to appendices. Dedicated limitations, future-work, and impact passages are added.

P2.justification: V1's single-column presentation becomes a two-column main text and bibliography with single-column appendices, conference-style front matter, and running headers. V3 adds Figure 1, a diagram connecting natural-deduction and Lean proof steps to MDP components. Equations and theorem displays are extensively reformatted.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially improves the coherence of the central learning guarantee: v1's Theorem 6 specifies squared-loss regression, while Appendix F switches to a net-extension estimator and additional assumptions; v3 aligns its explicit minimax estimator, coverage assumptions, and proof. The detailed occupancy argument and explicit oracle-label and candidate-retention limitations further strengthen precision. The narrower planner scope and abbreviated certificate development reduce breadth, but the improved support for the main theoretical result outweighs those losses.
